tasks.title: Add public ByteStats counter to the library
tasks.description: In src/lib.rs add `pub fn ByteCategory::of(byte: u8) -> ByteCategory` and make the private `Byte::category()` call it, so the logic lives in one place. Also derive Debug and PartialEq on ByteCategory. Add `#[derive(Default, Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)] pub struct ByteStats { pub null: u64, pub ascii_printable: u64, pub ascii_whitespace: u64, pub ascii_other: u64, pub non_ascii: u64 }` with these methods: `pub fn add(&mut self, bytes: &[u8])`, `pub fn total(&self) -> u64`, and `pub fn write_summary<W: Write>(&self, w: &mut W) -> io::Result<()>`. `write_summary` writes a blank line and then exactly the 7 lines in the spec (Portuguese labels, `{:.1}` percentages, 0.0 when total is 0). Add unit tests in the existing `mod tests` of lib.rs. Do not change the behavior of Printer.
tasks.acceptance: ["ByteStats::add on b\"AB \\x00\\xff\" gives null=1, ascii_printable=2, ascii_whitespace=1, ascii_other=0, non_ascii=1, total=5", "write_summary for that input produces exactly \"\\nResumo:\\nTotal de bytes: 5\\nNULL: 1 (20.0%)\\nASCII imprimível: 2 (40.0%)\\nEspaço em branco ASCII: 1 (20.0%)\\nOutros ASCII: 0 (0.0%)\\nNão-ASCII: 1 (20.0%)\\n\"", "write_summary on empty stats prints Total de bytes: 0 and 0 (0.0%) for every category", "cargo test and cargo clippy --all-targets pass"]
tasks.note: Added public `ByteCategory::of` (now used by the private `Byte::category()`), derived Debug/PartialEq on ByteCategory, and added the `ByteStats` struct with `add`, `total` and `write_summary`, which writes the Portuguese summary in the spec's format. Added unit tests for the five-byte example input and for empty stats; Printer behavior is unchanged.

tasks.title: Add --resumo/-R flag and print the summary in main
tasks.description: In src/main.rs add a field to `Opt`: `#[arg(short('R'), long("resumo"))] resumo: bool`, with a doc comment that becomes its --help text (see spec). In `run()`, after the --length handling has built the boxed `reader`, wrap it in a small private `CountingReader<R: Read> { inner: R, stats: Rc<RefCell<ByteStats>> }` (or something similar) whose `read` calls `stats.add(&buf[..n])`. Use it only when `opt.resumo` is set, so the default path stays unchanged. After `printer.print_all(...)` returns, drop the printer, call `stats.write_summary(&mut stdout)` and flush. Import ByteStats from hexyl. Make sure no other flag already uses `-R`.
tasks.acceptance: ["`hexyl --help` lists `-R, --resumo`", "`printf 'AB \\0\\377' | hexyl -R --color=never` ends with the 7 summary lines from the spec, after the bottom border", "Without -R, output is identical to before (existing integration tests pass unchanged)", "`hexyl -R --length 4` on a file counts only 4 bytes", "cargo build --all-targets and cargo clippy --all-targets pass"]
tasks.note: I added the `-R/--resumo` flag. When it is set, the reader is wrapped in a `CountingReader` after `--skip`/`--length`, so only the bytes shown are counted, and the summary is printed to stdout after the normal output. Without the flag nothing changes. Tests for the new behaviour are in tests/resumo_tests.rs; I haven't run the build or tests, and the README and man page are not updated yet.

tasks.title: Integration tests for --resumo
tasks.description: In tests/integration_tests.rs add a `mod resumo` that follows the existing style (use super::hexyl, write_stdin, assert stdout). Tests: (1) stdin "AB \x00\xff" with `-R --color=never` → stdout ends with the exact summary block; (2) the same with `--resumo`, which must give the same output; (3) without the flag, stdout contains no "Resumo:" and matches the old output for the same input; (4) empty input with -R → "Total de bytes: 0" and all 0 (0.0%); (5) `--length` limits what is counted; (6) `--plain -R` still appends the summary. Avoid inputs whose percentages are exact .x5 ties.
tasks.acceptance: ["all new tests pass with cargo test", "existing tests still pass"]
tasks.note: I added a `mod resumo` block to `tests/integration_tests.rs` with the six requested tests, written in the existing style. They cover `-R`, `--resumo`, running without the flag, empty input, `--length` and `--plain`, and none of the expected percentages is a .x5 tie. I haven't run them.
